My XXXX Prius was repossessed more than 6 weeks ago. I telephoned Toyota Financial Services ( TFS ) for guidance. I was told to wait for their letter. The letter came about a week later, and I read it. In accordance with that letter, I sent a check for the payoff amount ( {$2500.00} ). The check was sent \ return receipt requested. '' I received the return receipt indicating that on XXXX XXXX, a TFS employee ( " XXXX ) in XXXX XXXX, Iowa signed for the check. 
Nothing happened. I telephoned TFS at a their phone bank in Arizona, as directed in the letter, and inquired repeatedly about my vehicle. Each phone call requires anywhere from 22-42 minutes of waiting time. Each person who answered the phone could not tell me what the status of the check was or the status of the Prius. Indeed, I was advised that I had to find out what TFS in Iowa was doing with the check. ( I 'm in DC and not associated in any way with TFS. ) I telephoned a Toyota dealership near where I live ( XXXX Toyota in XXXX ), and asked for their assistance. I was told to send a cashier 's check and that was all that was needed. 
Just before going to get a cashier 's check, I checked my bank account. The check sent to Iowa was finally processed. At the time the check was processed, three weeks had elapsed. 
At this time, I can not get TFS to release the car. Indeed, I can not get anyone to tell me what the status is of my car. AND in the interim, I am told that the repossession company who took the car is charging me a daily fee plus towing fees, and other fees. 
I am XXXX years old. I am relying on friends and neighbors while trying to get my Prus back. At this time, however, I have no belief that I will get my car back. 
Please help."
